title: Talking About Pets & Animals
description: Build vocabulary for common domestic pets, farm animals, and verbs used to describe pet care.
objectives: Name common pets (cat, dog, bird, fish, rabbit) and farm animals (horse, cow, goat)
Use animal action verbs (feed, walk, bark, purr, play) in the present simple
Form complete sentences describing pet care routines and animal habits

vocabularyList.definition: A small domesticated carnivorous mammal with soft fur and retractable claws.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Our pet cat purrs when she is happy.

vocabularyList.definition: A domesticated carnivorous mammal known for loyalty and barking.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He walks his pet dog every morning.

vocabularyList.definition: A warm-blooded egg-laying vertebrate distinguished by feathers and wings.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: A colourful bird sings in the tree outside.

vocabularyList.definition: A limbless cold-blooded vertebrate animal with gills and fins living wholly in water.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: They have gold fish swimming in a small aquarium.

vocabularyList.definition: A large plant-eating domesticated mammal with solid hooves and a flowing mane.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: My uncle keeps a magnificent Arabian horse.

vocabularyList.definition: A gregarious burrowing plant-eating mammal with long ears and long hind legs.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The white rabbit loves fresh carrots.

vocabularyList.definition: To give food to an animal or person.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: I feed the birds every morning after breakfast.

vocabularyList.definition: The sharp explosive cry of a dog.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The guard dog barks when strangers approach.

vocabularyList.definition: The hindmost part of an animal, especially when prolonged beyond the rest of the body.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The friendly dog wags its tail.

vocabularyList.definition: Having or showing a mild, kind, or tender temperament.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Our pet cat is very gentle with small children.

sections.title: Pet Care & Animal Descriptions
sections.content:
Talking about pets combines **possession (have/has)**, **habits (present simple verbs)**, and **appearance adjectives**.

### Pronouns for Animals
- In general, animals take the neutral pronoun **it**.
- When an animal is a cherished family pet, native speakers often use **he** or **she** (*My cat Snow... she is very playful*).

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Common domestic animals: cat, dog, bird, rabbit, fish, horse.
Action verbs: feed (food), walk (exercise), bark (dog sound), purr (cat sound).
The plural of fish is fish (never fishes when counting).
Remember third-person singular verb rules for animals (The cat purrs, the dog barks).
Use 'it' for general animals, or 'he/she' for beloved family pets.
